subject: Getting a constant plot area with a variable number of axis label lines

messages.author: f6aff3ab0165e685
messages.subject: Getting a constant plot area with a variable number of axis label lines
parts:
Is there a way to fix the plot (data) area at a constant width and height? In the following example I have fixed the plot window, but if I vary the number of lines in the margin, the plot (data) area shinks.  In the example I am using x11(), but in practice I will be using ggsave().

p<-ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=cyl))+
  geom_point()+
  xlab("label")+
  ylab("label on two lines")
x11(width=3, heigh=3)
p

p+ylab("label on three lines")
x11(width=3, heigh=3)
p

Thanks,
Thomas

messages.author: dd68a26ecdacedb8
messages.subject: Re: Getting a constant plot area with a variable number of axis label lines
parts:
One approach is the theme() function with with a plot.margin= element. 

p1 <- ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=cyl)) +
  geom_point() +
  xlab("label") +
  ylab("label on two lines") +
  theme(plot.margin = unit(c(1,1,1,2.0), "cm"))
p1
p2 <- ggplot(data=mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=cyl)) +
  geom_point() +
  xlab("label") +
  ylab("label on three lines") +
  theme(plot.margin = unit(c(1,1,1,1.55), "cm"))
p2
ggsave("plot-1.png", plot=p1, scale=0.8)
ggsave("plot-2.png", plot=p2, scale=0.8)

In my RStudio environment and then viewing the .png files in a viewer, a difference in the plot area is not detectable to my eye.

-Phil
